svg.title: Orbit Remote trust boundaries
svg.desc: Computer A, the viewer, runs sandboxed Orbit windows, a main process and its own local Orbit host; computer B runs a remote listener, session services and the signed-in desktop. Numbered checks: 1, the IPC bridge between windows and the main process; 2, the main process pins the host certificate before the first byte, re-checks the TLS suite and checks every field the host sends; 3, the loopback local control channel with a per-launch bearer token, browser and DNS-rebinding refusal and a child proof; 4, Tailscale, which lets only tailnet nodes reach port 47832 over WireGuard, inside which Orbit runs mutual TLS; 5, the remote listener applies a connection cap, mutual TLS and link policy, a rate limit, the source check and the certificate pin; 6, per-request authority: owner block, grants, session ownership and resume epoch; 7, the operating system boundary: Orbit runs as the signed-in user with no shell or elevation.
